title: Reproduction Blueprint v1 (reproduction-blueprint-v1)
description: Structural contract for the plan the Baseline Reproduction Agent authors when a comparison method has no official code; `comparison reproduce` validates it, scaffolds the worktree from it and hashes the algorithm block into a fingerprint. methodId is echoed by the model but overwritten by the platform (parseBlueprintOutput), so an id mismatch is never a structural question. What is checked: the six top-level keys the prompt's output shape declares, algorithm.dataInterface and algorithm.metrics (the reproduce phases cannot run without them), and the two vocabularies the prompt itself enumerates — confidence and metric direction. What is deliberately NOT checked: that paperExplicit statements really appear in the papers, that assumptions are not smuggled into paperExplicit, that metric names equal the locked protocol's, that missingDetails are honest or that a claim of equivalence with official code is absent — those need the evidence context and stay in validateReproductionBlueprint (src/comparison/reproduce.ts:62). No minItems: the TS validator's "at least one paper-explicit statement" and "at least one metric" rules stay there, and a blueprint that fails them is a science gap reported to the user, not a shape error. algorithm.source/entry/hyperparameters are declared by the prompt but optional in the contract: the platform has defaults (--code, ['python','reproduce.py']) and refusing them would abort a run it can still serve.

source.description: The prompt says to leave it empty: a plan, not a program.
